newsitem.title: ITALY: NATO's Solana sees new IFOR mission.
newsitem.headline: NATO's Solana sees new IFOR mission.

text.p: NATO Secretary General Javier Solana said on Monday he hoped a NATO-led peace implementation force could remain in Bosnia next year to safeguard reconstruction.
"I hope we will have a force ready to continue overseeing reconstruction and economic rebuilding," Solana told reporters after talks with Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini.
Asked how long any new mandate for the IFOR force should be Solana said: "Nothing has been defined yet."
NATO sources said last month that the alliance would soon present detailed plans to commit thousands of troops to Bosnia next year after IFOR's mandate expires in December.
NATO sources said the 18 non-NATO countries in IFOR had expressed no objections to staying on in a new mission.
Any new peace force is expected to number several thousand below the 58,000-strong mission sent to oversee implementation of the Dayton peace accords which ended Bosnia's 43-month war.
Solana, in Rome to address the general assembly of the Atlantic Treaty Association which lasts until November 7, said Dini had expressed Italy's willingness to contribute to a new peacekeeping force.
